call_sites: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3477-3479 — _peer_command now reads the fleet gate before dispatching the __supervise__ role to _supervisor_command, so the direct module entry that starts a per-run supervisor is held as LanePaused like every other launch boundary. This is the only production call site the gained commit adds; the rest of the delta is the widened AST search in tests/test_the_fleet_gate_holds_dispatch.py (_assert_primitive_launch_paths_reach_gate and the legacy-supervisor case of test_worker_spawn_boundaries_hold_and_admit).

findings.text: follow-on: the widened primitive search collects a worker launch only when the process is started by a call whose name is `Popen` and whose argv derives from a `LaunchPlan`-typed parameter, a parameter named `plan`, a value subscripted `["plan"]`, or the `_worker_process_environment` env argument (lines 504-570). A launch path that starts a worker through another process primitive escapes the search even though it starts a worker: appending `def _probe_ungated_run(plan): subprocess.run(plan.argv)` to reckon/crew/resumption.py leaves test_launch_callers_reach_the_shared_gate green (reproduced at /tmp/rev-gate-scratch: 1 passed, EXIT=0), while the Popen twin of the same function reddens it (reproduced: 1 failed, EXIT=1, naming `ungated worker launch root: ('reckon/crew/resumption.py', '_probe_ungated_spawn')`). So the delta closes the prior review's name-keyed gap for Popen and covers the detached supervisor and fleet handoff, but the forward guarantee of §6 bullet 2 states, the predicate is still keyed on one primitive name, so a subprocess.run / os.posix_spawn / os.execv launch path would not be held to the gate read. No such path exists in the tree today, so this does not block landing; extending the predicate to the process-start primitives, or asserting the covered set of primitive names in §6, would close it.

justifications.durability: The new guard is load-bearing and I falsified it two ways. (1) Removing the single _require_fleet_gate_open() call from _peer_command's __supervise__ branch reddens test_worker_spawn_boundaries_hold_and_admit[legacy-supervisor] (reproduced at /tmp/rev-gate-scratch: 1 failed, EXIT=1, "DID NOT RAISE LanePaused"), and the restored tree passes the whole parametrised case (4 passed, EXIT=0). (2) Appending an ungated primitive caller to reckon/crew/resumption.py reddens test_launch_callers_reach_the_shared_gate by name (reproduced: 1 failed, EXIT=1), while the unmodified tree passes (1 passed, EXIT=0). The run's own primitive-negative-control.log records the same red. I did not find the guard passing its own test by disabling itself.
justifications.evidence: The reviewed run carries both arms on disk: gate-head.log names revision 220eb563 and reports 202 passed EXIT=0 (no failure id); after-suite.log names 3f36e54bf and reports 115 passed EXIT=0; followon-after-suite.log names 35706b3f (the gained head) and reports 116 passed EXIT=0. justifications.fit: The delta extends the existing search rather than adding a parallel mechanism: _assert_primitive_launch_paths_reach_gate reuses the module's existing _call_name and the new _worker_popen_calls / _direct_calls helpers, and the production change reuses the existing _require_fleet_gate_open()/LanePaused, adding a read that turns the legacy supervisor entry into the same held-as-a-wait behaviour as every other launch boundary. The legacy-supervisor case sits inside the existing test_worker_spawn_boundaries_hold_and_admit fixture.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §6: the delta routes the direct supervisor entry through the one gate read and makes the launch-path search trace worker process primitives to their callers and require a preceding gate read, so an appended ungated primitive caller now fails (reproduced). Coverage now spans the detached worker, the supervisor's own child spawn, the detached supervisor and the fleet handoff, with the watcher, budget-probe, shadow-picker and health-sampler subprocesses excluded by explicit assertions. The remaining shortfall is that the primitive name is fixed to Popen (finding).
justifications.reuse: No new abstraction: one guard call is added to an existing function, and the test gains one helper (_assert_primitive_launch_paths_reach_gate) composed of two small AST utilities that share the existing _call_name; the fixtures and pause/open controls are reused. Nothing is duplicated.
